sections.title: The Short Answer
sections.content:
The table below names 59 encounters across eight regions - 31 on the story path and 25 optional or recurring. S-GAME's own figure is 50 or more bosses, so this list is close to the full roster but not guaranteed to be every optional duel in the game.

This page replaced an older version that listed 11 bosses and labelled the rest unanswerable. That version was honest for its date - it was written before the 29 October 2026 release, when the only evidence was demos and trailers. The release made the question answerable, so the pre-launch roster is gone rather than kept alongside.

What is still not documented: elemental weaknesses and resistances for most fights. The game does have elemental interactions - water attacks strip Flame's fire, frost builds on you against the Blizzard Blademaster - but no outlet has published a per-boss weakness table, and this page will not invent one. Strategy per fight lives on the boss guide.

sections.title: Mirage Estate
sections.content:
Mirage Estate sits between the Mountain of Imprisonment and the Mount Soulrend climb. It is the region most often left out of published rosters, which is why the boss count in circulation drifts between 50 and 62.

BossTypeWhereDrop
Lei DangStoryMirage EstateTiger Cannon
Qiu Feng, the Crimson Boneblade (赤骨刀 邱风)StoryMirage EstateNot documented
Mo Yuan (莫渊)OptionalMirage EstateSoul Tempering material

Lei Dang is the only required fight here and is the source of the Tiger Cannon. Mo Yuan is optional and tied to Soul Tempering materials rather than a weapon drop, so skipping him costs upgrades rather than story.

sections.title: What Bosses Drop, and Why It Matters
sections.content:
Every boss that matters drops its weapon, and the pattern is consistent enough to plan around: the fight teaches the weapon. Beat Hua Qianxiao and you get The Fanatic's Broken Blade, a sword you drink from to make it fly. Beat Hua, Deadly Betrothed and you get the Scarlet Wraithblade, which lets Soul grow spider lilies the way she did. Beat Flame and you get the Flaming Mane, fire against the frost you will meet later.

That is why this list doubles as a weapon checklist. Five weapons in the roster above are not drops at all - they are found on racks or created by Tempering - and those are marked in the weapon guide instead: Jagged Steel, Bonesaw, Tianxuan Bronze Sword, Soft Snake Sword and the four Sanguine transformations.

Sources disagree on two entries and the tables follow the more specific one: Freezing Chaos is listed by one checklist as a drop from Yucong, No. 34 and by another as a Crimson Forest pickup at the Threadbound Great Tree; The Fanatic's Broken Blade is listed as Hua Qianxiao's drop and also as a Crimson Forest pickup. In both cases the boss and the region are the same place, so the practical answer does not change.

sections.title: The Optional Fights You Should Not Skip
sections.content:
Four optional bosses are load-bearing for the true ending, which makes 'optional' misleading:

  • The Gold-Masked One - five duels, one per Lóng Pillar. Losing leaves the pillar standing.
  • Blizzard Blademaster - drops Whiteshadow, and sits in the Illusion Realm behind the four-mask gate. Acolyte Guhe's mask is in the same region, so the two steps chain.
  • The four Acolytes - Yanru, Lei Ting, Guhe, Hansui. Their masks are the key to the Meigu Lake mirror.
  • Crimson Manor's secret boss - one of the two Crystal Puppet Eyes.

The full dependency chain is on the true ending checklist. For the fights themselves, the three habits that hold across the whole roster: parry the blue flash, dodge the red flash, and swap weapons to refill Sha-Chi instead of backing off.

sections.title: How Many Bosses Are There, Really
sections.content:
Three numbers circulate and they measure different things. S-GAME's director said 50 or more before release. This page names 56 distinct encounters. Trophy lists imply a fourth count by grouping fights: the The Four Freed trophy covers Yuzan, Yubi, Yuding and Yucong as one entry, Three Wardens Fall covers Cavalrybane, Soulclaimer and Heartpiercer as one, and Master of the Misty Waters groups You Loong, Yan Qiansui and the One-Eyed Archer.

So the roster is comfortably above 50 once rematches and Challenge Rift variants are counted, and any single published number below that is probably counting trophies rather than fights.

Names that route to more than one page are collected separately: Seven-Stars covers the formation, the Chief Disciple and the trophy, because all three turn up in the same search.

sections.title: Sources
sections.content:
Regional roster: NoobFeed's all-bosses guide, which is the only source found that organises the full set by region. Drops: AxeeTech's 51-item weapon checklist, Gamer.org's location guide and Quora Marketing's Pangzhen-specific list. Chinese names: 游侠网's all-boss strategy compilation and OSLink's main-line boss table. Trophy groupings: Game8 and Fextralife.

Every boss above appears in at least two of those sources except the ones marked Not documented for drops, which appear in the roster but in no loot list.
